help.intro1: The search interface is made of three sections: **Search**, **Explore**, and **Results**. These are described in detail below.
help.intro2: You may start searching either from the **Search** section or from the **Explore** section.
help.searchDesc: This section shows your current search criteria and allows you to submit keywords to search in the community.
help.search1: Each new submission adds the entered keywords to the list of search criteria.
help.search2: To start a new search instead of adding keywords to the current search, use the **Remove Filter** button, then enter your new keywords.
help.search3: To replace an already submitted keyword, first remove it by unchecking its checkbox, then submit a new keyword.
help.search4: You may control the extent of your search by selecting where to search. The options are:
help.search5: **In Authors Or Contributors:** Search your keywords in author or contributor names.
help.search6: **In Titles:** Search your keywords in titles.
help.search7: **In All Fields:** Search your keywords in all bibliographic record fields.
help.search8: **In Documents:** Search your keywords in the text content of the available documents.
help.search9: You may use boolean operators with your keywords. For instance:
help.search10: **AND:** Finds entries that contain all specified terms. This is the default relation between terms when no operator is specified, e.g., A B is the same as A AND B.
help.search11: **OR:** Finds entries that contain any of the specified terms, e.g., A OR B.
help.search13: Boolean operators must be entered in uppercase.
help.search14: You may use logical groupings (with parentheses) to eliminate ambiguities when using multiple boolean operators, e.g., (A OR B) AND C.
help.search15: You may require exact sequences of words (with double quotes), e.g., "A B C". The default difference between word positions is 1, meaning that an entry will match if it contains the words next to each other, but a different maximum distance may be specified (with the tilde character), e.g., "Web Search"~2 allows up to 1 word between Web and Search, meaning it could match web site search as well as web search.
help.exploreDesc: This section allows you to explore categories associated with the references.
help.explore1: Categories can be used to filter your search. Check a category to add it to your search criteria and narrow your search. Your search results will then only show entries that are associated with that category.
help.explore2: Uncheck a category to remove it from your search criteria and broaden your search results.
help.explore3: The numbers shown next to the categories indicate how many entries are associated with each category in the current set of results. Those numbers will vary based on your search criteria to always describe the current set of results. Likewise, categories and whole facets will disappear when the result set has no entries associated to them.
help.explore4: An arrow icon (v) appearing next to a category indicates that subcategories are available. You may press it to expand a list of more specific categories. You may press it again later to collapse the list. Expanding or collapsing subcategories will not change your current search; this allows you to quickly explore a hierarchy of categories if desired.
help.resultsDesc: This section shows the search results. When no search criteria has been given, it shows the full content of the bibliography (up to 20 entries per page).
help.results1: Each entry of the results list is a link to its full bibliographic record. From the bibliographic record view, you may continue exploring the search results by going to previous or following records in your search results, or you may return to the list of results.
help.results3: The **Abstracts** button lets you toggle the display of abstracts within the list of search results. Enabling abstracts, however, will have no effect on results for which no abstract is available.
help.results5: The **Relevance** sort is only available after keywords have been submitted using the **Search** section.
help.results6: Categories selected in the **Explore** section have no effect on the relevance score. Their only effect is to filter the list of results.

method.title: How types are read
method.when: Each record's type is set by AI when it enters the community; an editor can change it.

ai.lead: AI picks the one type that fits best.
ai.text: It reads the title and abstract, or only the title when a record has no abstract.

tie.text: A systematic review that pools its results counts as a meta-analysis, and a study that adds numbers to interviews or case studies as qualitative.

named.lead: Meta-analysis and randomised trial must be named.
named.text: The AI is offered them only when the title, abstract or PDF says so.

unsure.lead: Under 60% sure, a type is marked uncertain.
unsure.text: It is read again from the PDF once the record has one.

record.lead: Some records are typed without AI.
record.text: Datasets, software, corrections and registered protocols are typed from the record itself.

method.editor: An editor can correct any type.
method.several: Choosing several types shows records of any of them.

review-of-reviews.label: Review of reviews
review-of-reviews.description: Gathers and sums up earlier reviews or meta-analyses, such as an umbrella review.
review-of-reviews.not: Not a review of individual studies, which is a systematic or narrative review.

meta-analysis.label: Meta-analysis
meta-analysis.description: The authors statistically pool results from several earlier studies themselves. Quoting someone else's pooled result does not count. Given only when the title, abstract or PDF says so.
meta-analysis.not: Not a review that quotes someone else's pooled result or doesn't pool at all, which is a systematic or narrative review.

systematic-review.label: Systematic review
systematic-review.description: Sums up earlier studies found with a stated search and inclusion rules, without pooling them. Includes scoping and rapid reviews.
systematic-review.not: Not a review that pools results, which is a meta-analysis, or one with no stated search, which is a narrative review.

literature-review.label: Narrative review
literature-review.description: A narrative, critical or integrative review with no stated search method.
literature-review.not: Not a review with a stated search and inclusion rules, which is a systematic review.

bibliometric.label: Bibliometric study
bibliometric.description: Counts and maps publications, authors or citations on a topic, rather than what the studies found.
bibliometric.not: Not a review of what the studies found, which is a systematic or narrative review.

rct.label: Randomised trial
rct.description: Participants, groups or places were randomly assigned to conditions. Given only when the title, abstract or PDF says so.
rct.not: Not a comparison without random assignment, which is a quasi-experiment, or a review of trials.

quasi-experiment.label: Quasi-experiment
quasi-experiment.description: An intervention compared with a comparison group chosen without random assignment.
quasi-experiment.not: Not a study with random assignment, which is a randomised trial, or one with no comparison group, which is a quantitative study.

quantitative.label: Quantitative study
quantitative.description: Surveys, correlational and observational studies, single-group before-and-after tests, analyses of existing data.
quantitative.not: Not a comparison of assigned groups, which is a trial or quasi-experiment, or the building or testing of a model, which is a modelling study.

qualitative.label: Qualitative or mixed methods
qualitative.description: Interviews, focus groups, case studies, ethnography or document analysis, alone or with quantitative data.
qualitative.not: Not numbers alone, with no interviews, cases or documents, which is a quantitative study.

modelling.label: Modelling study
modelling.description: Builds, simulates, projects or tests a model, method, tool or system, judged on how well it performs.
modelling.not: Not statistics on collected data without building or testing a model, which is a quantitative study.

protocol.label: Protocol
protocol.description: A study or review that is planned or under way, with no results yet.
protocol.not: Not a study that reports results.

commentary.label: Commentary
commentary.description: An editorial, opinion, policy analysis, theory or framework with no new data.
commentary.not: Not a paper with new data, or a review of studies.

not-research.label: Other
not-research.description: A dataset, software, correction, book review, or a file that accompanies another paper.
not-research.not: Not an opinion or policy piece, which is a commentary.
